summary.text: The next-of-kin must apply for a grant of letters of administration, then approach the Public Trustee's Office.

details.heading: Where the CPF savings go
details.body: Without a CPF nomination, the CPF savings are transferred to the Public Trustee's Office for distribution to family members under intestacy laws or inheritance laws for Muslims.

details.heading: Administrative fee
details.body: The Public Trustee's Office charges an administrative fee for this service.

steps.name: Apply for administration
steps.text: Apply for a grant of letters of administration.

steps.name: Approach the PTO
steps.text: After applying, approach the Public Trustee's Office to proceed with the CPF distribution.

example_phrasings: What happens to CPF without a will or nomination?
If the deceased had no will or CPF nomination, will CPF contact the next-of-kin?

sources.page_title: If the deceased passed on without a will and did not make a CPF nomination. Will CPF contact the next-of-kin directly or do we need to appoint an administrator ourselves?

quotes.text: The next-of-kin would have to apply for a grant of letters of administration and approach PTO to proceed with the distribution.
The next-of-kin would have to apply for a grant of letters of administration
and approach PTO to proceed with the distribution.

If a member did not make a CPF nomination, upon his/her passing, his/her CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution to family members under intestacy laws or inheritance laws (for Muslims).
PTO will charge an administrative fee for this service.
